ctx.x: From the press people, yeah. Because your heart is where your money is, and they're making their living there. And so there seems to be a separation now. There's a coolness that's coming. But more than that, think of the tragedy of the great clarinetists, Jimmy Noone, who never made number one on the poll.

They become thrown in the ashcan. That's the whole style. And ten years of their lives is taken away from them, because if you don't work, if you -- did you ever read the liner notes that Studs Terkel wrote for Columbia Artists on Big Bill Broonzy's appearance in Niagara or some town? Studs loaned it to me. He's booed by his own people, he's booed out, because of the music. He's old-fashioned, he's old hat.

I worked the Capital Lounge in Chicago, and I got what we call a Dixieland setup, clarinet, trombone and trumpet. But I got Buddy Smith on drums. Buddy has played with Diz, he's played with the Bird, he's played with Zut and now he's playing with me. He's a good drummer.
